name: Cloud & DevOps
blurb: Ship and run apps: hosting choice, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Azure and observability.
searches: GitHub Actions security OIDC best practice update
Cloudflare Workers Cloud Run Lambda new feature announcement
Kubernetes release deprecation pod security change
agent skill DevOps deploy Claude Terraform Kubernetes

tests.prompt: Write a production Dockerfile and .dockerignore for a Node 22 Express API that builds TypeScript to dist/, then give me the gcloud commands to deploy it to Cloud Run in europe-west1 with a secret API key.
tests.good: Multi-stage build with pinned slim/alpine base, deps cached before source copy, dev deps excluded, numeric non-root user, listens on 0.0.0.0 and $PORT; .dockerignore excludes .git, node_modules and .env; builds for linux/amd64; deploy uses Artifact Registry image, explicit --region, dedicated service account, --set-secrets from Secret Manager (not env literal), asks before --allow-unauthenticated; verification via logs and health check; rollback via traffic to previous revision.

tests.prompt: Set up GitHub Actions for our Terraform repo (AWS, two environments). PRs should show the plan, merges to main should apply to prod.
tests.good: fmt -check, validate, tflint and a security scan (trivy/checkov) on PRs; plan -out uploaded as artifact and summarised on the PR; apply consumes the reviewed plan file (no re-plan) in a protected production environment with required reviewers; AWS auth via OIDC with aud sts.amazonaws.com and sub pinned to repo and branch/environment (no wildcards), no static keys; remote S3 state with locking and separate state per env; pinned versions and committed lock file; scheduled drift detection that alerts rather than auto-applies.

tests.prompt: Our Kubernetes deployment shows pods in CrashLoopBackOff right after a new release. Walk me through finding the cause and getting users back to working.
tests.good: Mitigates first with kubectl rollout undo (or previous image) and checks rollout status; then diagnoses with describe pod events, logs --previous, events sorted by time; checks exit code (137 OOMKilled vs app error), missing env/secret, wrong command/port, overly aggressive liveness probe; compares the diff between releases; suggests readiness/startup probes and resource limits; no destructive steps without confirmation.
